decisions.reason: Baseline alignment is a separate requirement independently introduced by the same message; tighter optical spacing does not change its alignment rule.
The same-message introduction already records optical spacing as a comparison dimension; the detailed spacing direction remains owned by the kerning requirement.
Tighter spacing changes placement between letterforms, not the E and L construction, geometry, scale, or architectural design requirements.
The optical-spacing adjustment does not alter the selected all-caps case treatment.
The spacing direction does not change the second V's height relationships or hierarchy role.
Changing optical spacing across the word does not modify the approved Hero V geometry or its design attributes.
The source preserves the second V construction; it only requests a different spacing composition around the letterforms.
The tighter-spacing request does not change the É accent's required literal derivation from the Hero V terminal.
The composition and kerning exploration does not resume or modify the deferred champagne-gold material treatment.
Optical spacing does not change the required shared peak horizon between the Hero V and É accent.
Exploring kerning does not unlock or alter the signature assets and is compatible with varying only the composition currently under review.
The spacing decision does not change the requirement to explain each design round's rationale.
